answer: Karst Anchor Delay. Each new identity must complete a slow, publicly logged task tied to a physical resource—say, provisioning a unique hardware token that takes days to ship—before it can transact. The token's serial is bound to a karst-like chain of prior registrations, so cloning branches split the same scarce shipment window. An attacker's marginal clone now costs a real token plus a multi-day stall, while its expected payoff is capped by the parent's reputation decay. A single comet of activity can't hide the lag. Willow-grade patience is required per identity,
